summary.text: A 60-year-old man was admitted with severe low back pain for more than 10 years and progressive left lower limb radicular pain and numbness in the last week. VAS was 8, JOA 11 and ODI 64%, with left lower extremity hypoesthesia, 4/5 strength of the left quadriceps and first toe, positive left Lasegue sign at 30° and a weakened left knee reflex.

MRI and CT showed left nerve roots compressed by an L2-3 herniated disc with a large free nucleus pulposus dissociated upward; extension and flexion X-ray showed no spinal instability and CT showed no disc calcification. After failure of conservative treatment he underwent PELD with IONM under general anesthesia.

Monitoring showed decreased MEP amplitude in the compressed nerve root and no abnormal frEMG signals, then an immediate increase in MEP amplitude after the free nucleus pulposus was removed. Postoperative MRI showed the disc fragment removed and the left nerve root decompressed, with no nerve root injury.

On awakening his back and leg pain was relieved and VAS fell from 8 to 0; he got out of bed and was discharged the next day. One month after surgery VAS was 0; JOA scores of 23 and an ODI of 24% are also reported without a stated time. At one year outpatient follow-up there was no pain, numbness was greatly improved, and no complication or recurrence was observed.
